summary_en: Dai Nippon Toryo will acquire all issued shares of Shinto Toryo through a simplified stock exchange, making it a wholly owned subsidiary. The exchange is scheduled to become effective on February 2026, with Shinto Toryo shares delisting from Tokyo Stock Exchange Standard Market on the same date.
title_en: Notice Regarding Conclusion of Stock Exchange Agreement for Making Shinto Toryo Company, Limited a Wholly Owned Subsidiary of Dai Nippon Toryo Company, Limited (Simplified Stock Exchange)
translation_en_brief:
Dai Nippon Toryo Company, Limited and Shinto Toryo Company, Limited have concluded a stock exchange agreement under which Dai Nippon Toryo will be the parent company and Shinto Toryo will become a wholly owned subsidiary. The transaction will be implemented as a simplified stock exchange under Article 796(2) of the Companies Act and does not require approval by shareholder meetings of Dai Nippon Toryo. The effectiveness of the stock exchange is scheduled for February 2, 2026 (planned), following approval by an extraordinary shareholder meeting of Shinto Toryo scheduled for January 2026. Shinto Toryo shares will delist from the Tokyo Stock Exchange Standard Market on February 2026.

Prior to this stock exchange, Dai Nippon Toryo launched a public tender offer for Shinto Toryo shares beginning February 7, 2025. Following completion of this public offer on March 2025, Shinto Toryo became a subsidiary of Dai Nippon Toryo through a third-party allotment increase in shares. The tender offer price was set at a discount from the market price prevailing around the announcement date of the subsidiary acquisition. General shareholders were given individual discretion regarding participation in the tender offer, and no general shareholders participated in the offer.

The transaction aims to expand Dai Nippon Toryo's paint business foundation. The Shinto Toryo Group provides high-quality, high-performance, and environmentally responsive paint products and coating materials and services backed by advanced technological capabilities, which aligns with Dai Nippon Toryo's basic strategy of acquiring and leveraging external resources in addition to internal growth.
